text:
alex: Heads-up — planning a terraform apply in the change window at 02:00 UTC for VPC + IAM updates. Provider will be pinned to 4.0.2. Need rollback path, canary, and owner for rollback decisions. Release notes link: https://redwood.internal/releases/rel-2026-03-21
maria: Ack. Post the plan summary and affected services when you have it?
alex: Plan summary: ~2 new routes, 1 natgw replace, 3 IAM role updates. Small risk to tenant routing. Snippet:
```bash
# terraform plan -out=canary.plan
+ aws_nat_gateway.main (new)
~ aws_route.private[*] (2 to add)
~ aws_iam_role.webhook (update)
```
sam: @alex recommend canary in us-west-2 only and enable fast rollback using provider pin + previous state snapshot. Snapshot ready: s3://infra-snapshots/2026-03-20/vpc-before-apply.tfstate
irene: ops-oncall will be monitoring. Please add alerts on route-table diffs and healthcheck failover.
ops-oncall: ops-oncall: I'll be in the channel during the window and watching CloudWatch + routing alarms.
deploybot: [deploybot] Preflight checks passed. plan validated, drift score low, no pending locks. Canaries allowed: us-west-2. Auto-fallback policy: provider-pin -> fallback-provider: aws-provider@4.0.1
alex: Proposal: two-step apply — (1) canary in us-west-2, (2) global rollout if canary OK. If canary fails, rollback to snapshot and revert IAM patch. Sound good?
maria: +1. I'll add a short release blurb: "networking: staged NAT gateway rollout; IAM: webhook role policy tightened (minor)"
sam: Set canary TTL 15m. If error rate >1% in canary -> rollback. Who triggers rollback? ops-oncall or infra lead?
ops-oncall: ops-oncall: I'll trigger rollback on threshold breach or manual. Deploybot manual override: `deploybot cancel --apply-id=1764444444-canary`
alex: I'll run the canary apply at 02:05 UTC and post the deploybot ID. Provider is pinned in backend to 4.0.2 and rollback docs are up to date.
deploybot: [deploybot] Canary started: apply-id=ddb-20260321-001, executing canary in us-west-2. ETA 4m.
alex: Note — NAT replacement can cause short ENI flaps; expect 1-2 min of transient routing noise. Ops: monitor BGP peers and health checks.
ops-oncall: Seen transient ENI flaps on earlier tests, watching CloudWatch, route53, and BGP metrics.
sam: Reminder: after canary success, run a tf state verify: `terraform state list | grep aws_route`
maria: Security review done and tagged; oncall rotation updated.
deploybot: [deploybot] Canary completed: success. apply-id=ddb-20260321-001. No errors. Plan applied: 3 resources added / 2 changed. Proceed with global? React :thumbsup: or :thumbsdown:
alex: :thumbsup:
ops-oncall: :thumbsup:
sam: :thumbsup:
maria: Go for global. Run in waves: us-west-2 -> us-east-1 -> eu-west-1.
deploybot: [deploybot] Global rollout started: rollout-id=ddb-20260321-002. Wave 1: us-west-2 -> done. Wave 2: us-east-1 -> in progress.
deploybot: [deploybot] Rollout completed successfully. release-note-id=rel-2026-03-21-ff
alex: Thanks all. We'll keep the provider pin for 48h and monitor cost/latency dashboards. Closing thread after 24h unless issues pop up.
